plain: This story starts at Roswell, New Mexico, where in 1947 something is said to have crashed. A US Army officer named Philip J. Corso wrote a book called The Day After Roswell. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in the book Corso claims a secret government group was set up under Admiral Roscoe Hillenkoetter, the first director of the CIA. According to Michels, Corso ran the Army's foreign technology desk and was given material from the crash to pass out quietly to private industry, mainly Bell Labs, a famous research laboratory. Michels says Corso thought the transistor, the tiny switch behind modern electronics, was reverse engineered from what was found. An online researcher known as UAPGerb tells it too, saying Corso described technologies being seeded into US defense companies around 1959 and 1960. Some tellings name Bell Labs, others speak more broadly, and one places the material at Wright-Patterson, an Air Force base. If true, everyday technology would owe part of its origin to a crashed craft.
